messages:
Maya Chen: heads-up — customer acme-ml opened a ticket: users get immediate re-auth prompts after SSO, mobile app shows 401 on requests that used to work. Started ~03:40 UTC after last-night cookie prune job. They're reporting device-trust never completes. :confused:
Samir Patel: do we have the ticket id? any customer repro steps?
Maya Chen: ticket #34218. Repro steps from them: 1) sign in via SAML SSO -> lands on consent screen; 2) desktop okay, but mobile goes to spinner then 'session expired' when calling /v1/user/profile; 3) if they re-open they get stuck in a redirect loop to company IdP. They said some users can log in on desktop but then get a cookie cleared on next load.
Linh Tran: sharing quick logs from their mobile session (redacted):
```
Request: GET /v1/user/profile
Headers: Cookie: session=eyJhbGci...; device_trust=1
Response: 401 Unauthorized
Set-Cookie: session=; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax
X-Auth-Error: invalid_session_cookie
```

Linh Tran: looks like session cookie was explicitly cleared by the prune job, even though device_trust header was present. Not sure why prune selected those cookies.
Samir Patel: deploy-bot ran a cron last night? @deploy-bot can you confirm job id/time?
support-bot: ticket 34218 created and linked to this thread. SLA priority 2.
deploy-bot: nightly-cookie-pruner ran at 2026-03-14T03:38:12Z (job id: prune-20260314-03). Targets: expired_sessions, stale_sessions. Matched 28k cookies, purged 4,220 active sessions flagged by TTL check.
Alex Rivera: do we have an instrumentation tag on sessions for device_trust or OAuth refresh tokens? The prune job should skip sessions with active device_bind.
Linh Tran: we added device_trust tag last year but prune job uses last_access + session_type; I think mobile sessions created via OAuth device flow have session_type="oauth_device" and TTL 7d. The job mistakenly matched them because a new cookie-rotation change replaced the cookie name from "session" -> "session_v2" and prune only recognized v1 flags. So prune didn't see the device_trust tag on v2 cookies.
Maya Chen: customer says only users with SSO + device-trust enabled on mobile are impacted. Desktop unaffected for many users.
Samir Patel: thanks. Can we repro internally? Linh, can you paste a curl that reproduces the 401?
Linh Tran: repro curl (redacted client_id):
```
curl -i -H "Cookie: session_v2=eyJ...; device_trust=1" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/user/profile
# returns 401 and Set-Cookie clearing session_v2
```

Linh Tran: also saw SAML assertion logs: Assertion consumed at 03:36:44Z, but session created with cookie name session_v2 at 03:36:44Z then prune job removed at 03:38:12Z. TTL and tag mismatch.
Alex Rivera: root cause hypothesis: cookie-rotation RFC landed in last deploy; we doubled cookie names and forgot to update the prune selector to accept session_v2. prune matched by prefix 'session' only and treated v2 as expired fallback.
Samir Patel: action items: 1) immediate hotfix to prune job to include session_v2; 2) backfill to re-issue sessions for impacted workspace or a targeted no-op to restore session cookies; 3) customer communication and remediation steps.
Maya Chen: customer asks for temporary workaround they can do while we fix. Any manual steps?
Linh Tran: simple workaround: have affected users sign out from all devices then sign back in — that will create fresh session_v2 cookies. But for those stuck in redirect loop to IdP they can't sign out easily. We can issue a server-side one-time session reset for the workspace (force new session cookie on next login).
eng-runtime: adding @eng-runtime. We need an emergency patch to skip v2 cookies in prune or make prune check cookie metadata instead of name. Who can own?
Alex Rivera: I can take the patch. Will open a PR to: a) add session_v2 to whitelist, b) add guard to skip cookies with device_trust tag regardless of name. Plan to ship hotfix within 60 minutes if approved.
Samir Patel: please post PR link then run canary on staging and one region. Notify support when done so we can tell customer.
Alex Rivera: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/+/D2345 (draft) — tests added. Running staging canary now.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started: infra-prune-fix v2 -> staging (canary=1%).
Linh Tran: I'll prepare a short repro script we can run to validate and a rollback plan. Also prepping DB query to list affected sessions by workspace id so we can target backfill.
Maya Chen: messaging to customer: "We're investigating: a nightly maintenance job accidentally cleared some mobile SSO sessions created after a cookie-rotation change. We have a hotfix deploying and can either trigger workspace-scoped session re-issue or walk users through a sign-out/sign-in. We're prioritizing your workspace and will update in 30 minutes." OK?
Samir Patel: good. Add: "We don't believe API keys or embeddings were affected; only web/mobile session cookies for interactive users."
Maya Chen: sent to customer, they acknowledged and gave permission to perform targeted session reset.
Alex Rivera: hotfix merged and deployed to staging, canary looks good (no regressions). Starting rollout to us-east-1 now.
deploy-bot: rollout: infra-prune-fix v2 -> us-east-1 (progress 0 -> 20% -> 100%).
Alex Rivera: deployed to us-east-1 and ran backfill: reissued 312 sessions for workspace acme-ml. I also rolled a lightweight migration to ensure prune selects cookie metadata not name.
Linh Tran: validated with the curl repro — mobile now returns 200 and retains session_v2 cookie.
Maya Chen: customer confirmed users can sign in now and device-trust completes. They reported no data exposure and thanked support. :white_check_mark:
Samir Patel: postmortem items: 1) update prune selectors and add unit tests for cookie name variants; 2) add monitoring alert when prune deletes >X sessions in <Y minutes for a single tenant; 3) run a one-off audit to find other jobs that assume cookie name prefixes.
eng-runtime: noted, will own 1 and 3. Also raise a security review about cookie-rotation assumptions.
Maya Chen: thanks team. Closing ticket when customer confirms stable for 24h.
support-bot: ticket 34218 updated: status -> resolved (pending 24h confirmation).
